# ICP: Maya Okafor's Career Change Clients

## 1. THE PERSON
Priya Nair is 41, a senior associate at a City law firm in London. She earns well, bills 2,100 hours a year and has been thinking about leaving for two years. She was passed over for partner in March and told herself it did not matter. It does. Her partner says follow your passion, which helps nobody.

## 2. WHAT THEY WANT
| | |
|---|---|
| Surface problem | I want a different job |
| Real problem | I have built a career I do not want and I feel trapped by my own salary |
| What they want to feel | Relief on a Monday morning |
| What solved looks like | A decision they can defend to their partner and a plan they believe |

## 3. HOW THEY BUY
| | |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Passed over for promotion, turning forty, a younger colleague made partner |
| Who else they consider | Career quizzes, a recruiter, an executive coach |
| Time to decide | Three to six weeks after the first call |

## 4. THEIR WORDS
- "I have built a career I do not want any more"
- "I feel trapped by my own salary"
- "I have no idea what else I could do"
- "Follow your passion helps nobody"
- "I am too senior to start again"
- "I would have to take a pay cut"
- "I keep opening LinkedIn and closing it"
- "Everyone thinks I have it sorted"
- "It is Sunday night and I feel sick"
- "I am forty and I still do not know what I want to be"

## 5. THE FIVE OBJECTIONS
1. It is too late for me at my level.
2. I would have to take a pay cut I cannot afford.
3. Coaching is a bit soft and I am a serious person.
4. I already tried a career quiz and it told me to be a librarian.
5. I cannot spare the time with the hours I work.

## 6. WHAT TO TALK ABOUT
- The Sunday night dread nobody admits to
- Why passion advice fails senior professionals
- How to test a new career without quitting first
